rules.name: Ephemeral or view model has many consumers
rules.short_description: An ephemeral or view model reaches the configured consumer threshold; review repeated transformation cost.
rules.long_description:
A view stores a query, and an ephemeral model becomes a CTE in each dependent model. Expensive logic can therefore be evaluated in several consumer queries. Actual cost depends on selected models, the query plan, and caching. A consumer count alone does not measure that cost.

The rule reports a view or ephemeral model with at least `ephemeral_fanout_threshold` model consumers. The default threshold of 3 is a local review setting, not a dbt requirement. Dependencies come from the `ref()` calls in each model file. A manifest is not used.

A table stores the result for reuse, but adds build and storage costs. It can also be less current than a view. Keep a view or ephemeral model when its transformations are cheap or the measured workload favors it.

References:
- [Materializations](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/materializations)
rules.remediation: Measure the transformation cost across representative consumers. Consider `materialized='table'` if reuse saves enough work and scheduled refresh meets freshness needs. Keep the current materialization when the data is small, the query is cheap, or freshness requires it. Record the reason rather than changing materialization solely to satisfy the threshold.

examples.title: Ephemeral or view model with many consumers

rules.name: Intermediate model has one consumer and limited metadata
rules.short_description: A silver or unclassified SQL model has one consumer and lacks a description together with tests or columns.
rules.long_description:
A single-consumer intermediate model can be useful for readability, testing, or ownership. dbt documents this pattern. The model is not redundant solely because it has one consumer.

This local review rule checks SQL models in the silver layer or with no recognized layer. It reports one model consumer unless the schema entry has both a description and at least one test or column entry. Dependencies come from the `ref()` calls in each model file. A manifest is not used. Column metadata alone does not prove that tests exist.

Consider a named CTE when the separate model adds no useful boundary. Keep the model when it isolates complex logic or defines an intentional interface.

References:
- [Intermediate: Purpose-built transformation steps](https://docs.getdbt.com/best-practices/how-we-structure/3-intermediate)
- [Materializations](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/materializations)
- [Add data tests to your DAG](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/data-tests)
rules.remediation: Check the purpose of the intermediate model. Keep and document it when the boundary helps maintainers. Add tests for its grain and business rules. If it only splits a simple query, consider a named CTE in the consumer. An ephemeral model can retain the separate file without creating a stored relation, but cannot be queried directly.

examples.title: Intermediate model with a single consumer
examples.bad:
-- silver/int_a.sql, used only by gold/fct_b.sql, no schema entry
select * from {{ ref('stg_a') }}
examples.good:
models:
  - name: int_a
    description: Deduplicated A records.
    columns:
      - name: id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]

rules.name: Clustering key exceeds the configured column limit
rules.short_description: cluster_by has more columns than max_cluster_columns; review the workload and maintenance cost.
rules.long_description:
Snowflake recommends no more than three or four columns or expressions in a clustering key for most tables. Additional keys can cost more to maintain than they save in query work. The useful key depends on the workload, data distribution, and column order.

The rule reports a table or incremental model whose `cluster_by` list exceeds `max_cluster_columns`. Its default of 4 is a configurable local threshold, not a Snowflake limit.

Snowflake can prune micro-partitions without an explicit clustering key. Do not add clustering solely because a filter exists, or remove a key solely because this rule reports it.

References:
- [Clustering Keys & Clustered Tables](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/tables-clustering-keys)
- [SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_INFORMATION](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/functions/system_clustering_information)
rules.remediation: Compare representative query profiles and clustering cost. Use `SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_INFORMATION` to review `average_depth` and `average_overlaps`. Favor columns used in selective filters; join, grouping, or sorting columns can also help. Check cardinality and key order. Keep extra columns only when measured benefits justify them.

rules.name: Model config repeats a folder value
rules.short_description: A model config() value equals the value inherited from its folder.
rules.long_description:
For scalar model settings, a model-level `config()` takes precedence over `dbt_project.yml`. Repeating an inherited value can therefore keep the old value after the folder default changes.

The rule compares model config values with resolved folder values. This is an equality check, not proof that the model setting has no purpose. Some settings, including hooks, accumulate rather than replace inherited values.

Keep an explicit value when the model must remain independent of future folder changes. Review cumulative settings separately before removing them.

References:
- [Model configurations](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/model-configs)
- [pre-hook & post-hook](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/resource-configs/pre-hook-post-hook)
rules.remediation: For scalar settings, remove a repeated model value if the model should follow the folder default. Keep it if the model must stay fixed. For hooks or other cumulative settings, inspect the effective configuration first; removing an entry can change the statements or values dbt applies.

examples.title: Model config repeats the folder default

rules.name: Layer folder has no explicit materialization default
rules.short_description: A top-level model folder has no +materialized setting on the folder or project node.
rules.long_description:
An explicit folder materialization can document a layer's intended behavior in one place. dbt does not require it: SQL models use views by default, and more specific model settings can override inherited values.

This local architecture rule reports a top-level model folder without `+materialized` on that folder or the project node. It does not establish that the models are misconfigured.

No change is needed when subfolders or individual models deliberately set the required materialization. Choose defaults from workload and access needs, not a fixed bronze/silver/gold recipe.

References:
- [Model configurations](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/model-configs)
- [Materializations](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/materializations)
rules.remediation: Review the effective settings for the listed folders. Add a `+materialized` default under the project's `models` entry only when a common setting is useful. For example, use `view` for cheap SQL transformations if current data is required. Keep specific overrides. Python models support table or incremental materialization, not view or ephemeral.

examples.title: Layer folder has no materialization default
examples.good:
models:
  demo:
    bronze:
      +materialized: ephemeral
    silver:
      +materialized: ephemeral
    gold:
      +materialized: table

rules.name: Build configuration depends on a variable
rules.short_description: A config() call inside a variable-dependent condition changes how the model builds.
rules.long_description:
A conditional `config()` can change model behavior when a variable changes. dbt supports variables and command-line overrides, so this pattern is not inherently invalid. Consolidation needs to preserve each supported invocation, not assume one fixed configuration.

The rule reports `config()` inside an `if` condition that reads `var()`, directly or through a detected variable assignment. It checks `materialized`, `incremental_strategy`, `unique_key`, `enabled`, `full_refresh`, `on_schema_change`, and `transient`. Hook-only gates belong to SSC-EWI-DBTINC0019.

Keep a deliberate switch when callers, accepted values, and resulting build modes are documented and tested.

References:
- [Project variables](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/project-variables)
- [Model configurations](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/model-configs)
- [full_refresh](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/resource-configs/full_refresh)
rules.remediation: Inspect project defaults and orchestration arguments before removing the condition. If the setting should be fixed, put it in an unconditional `config()` or a folder setting. If the switch is required, preserve it and test every supported mode, including full refresh. Record who supplies the variable and why the modes differ.

examples.title: Conditional config
